faq_pixel_question: Why do I need a first-generation Pixel?
faq_pixel_answer: This workflow uses an original Pixel or Pixel XL to upload to Google Photos. Google currently lists unlimited original-quality storage for first-generation Pixel phones; other generations have different rules. Check the settings and actual benefits on your phone and account first. PixelBridge neither provides nor guarantees Google’s storage service.
faq_icloud_question: Do I need to turn off Optimize Mac Storage?
faq_icloud_answer: No. Missing originals are downloaded from iCloud when needed. Photos must first appear in the Mac’s system photo library. Keep a network connection and enough disk space for staging and conversion.
faq_motion_question: Will a motion photo become a separate photo and video?
faq_motion_answer: Supported HEIC / JPEG Live Photos are packaged into one motion-photo file for Google Photos. Some paired videos are converted to H.264. Format compatibility varies, and Google may finish processing motion playback after the upload completes. Start with a small sample and check playback on the web and phone.
faq_cleanup_question: Are files on both Mac and Pixel cleaned up automatically?
faq_cleanup_answer: Only eligible Mac staging files are reclaimed automatically, after progress is saved and Pixel files are verified. Photos on Pixel are not deleted automatically. Confirm backup in Google Photos before using Free up space on the phone. Apple Photos originals and progress records are retained.
faq_dedup_question: Will freeing space on Pixel cause repeat transfers?
faq_dedup_answer: With the same computer, photo library and progress records, completed items are skipped even after their Pixel files are removed. This also means the current version will not automatically resend a Pixel file deleted before cloud backup.
faq_overnight_question: Can it run overnight? Does Pixel need to stay connected?
faq_overnight_answer: It can keep running, but USB must stay connected during transfers and Google Photos needs a network connection to upload. Keep the Mac awake. Closing the window leaves the menu-bar app running; quitting stops scheduling. Transfers pause at temperature or storage limits and automatic mode checks again later. Keep the devices ventilated and check an older phone’s battery condition regularly.
faq_progress_question: How should I preserve backup progress?
faq_progress_answer: Progress records let PixelBridge skip completed items and resume interrupted work. Quit before updating the app and retain its data folder. Do not delete the State folder as if it were photo cache. Photo-library identifiers can differ between computers, so copying progress does not guarantee duplicate detection with another library.

features_description_first: As your library grows, exporting, converting and copying take more work.
features_description_second: PixelBridge connects those steps to keep another copy of your existing library.
feature_habits_description: Keep using iPhone, Apple Photos and iCloud. When new photos reach the system library, the app discovers them and schedules transfers in automatic mode.
feature_motion_description: Package supported photos and paired videos into single motion-photo files. Ordinary photos and videos are transferred as unmodified originals.
feature_resume_title: Pick up where you left off
feature_resume_description: Completed items are skipped. Progress survives interruptions, and failed items retry according to the queue’s rules.

step_install_title: Install the app and allow photo access
step_install_description: Download the beta, unzip it and move it to Applications. Allow Apple Photos access and make sure the system library is syncing with iCloud. Optimize Mac Storage can stay on.
step_connect_title: Connect Pixel and enable Google Photos backup
step_connect_description: Enable Developer options and USB debugging on Pixel, connect it over USB, and authorize the computer on the phone. If ADB is missing, the app can guide its installation. Sign in to Google Photos and enable backup.
step_sample_title: Try Back up once with a small batch
step_sample_description: Transfer a few photos, motion photos and videos. Confirm they reached the phone, then check backup and motion playback in Google Photos on both the phone and the web.
step_automatic_title: Turn on automatic backup at your own pace
step_automatic_description: Set a batch size, check interval and cache budget. Keep the Mac awake and Pixel connected. The app keeps running in the menu bar after you close its window.
step_automatic_hint: Default: 10 items per batch · 5 minutes between rounds
care_kicker: A LITTLE CARE GOES A LONG WAY
care_description: Automation handles repetition. You stay in control of backup confirmation.
care_cache_description: After progress is saved and Pixel files are verified again, eligible Mac staging files are reclaimed. Files are kept if verification fails. Large files still need enough working space.
care_pixel_description: Phone files are not removed automatically. Confirm cloud backup, then use Free up space in Google Photos. Never delete files that have not been backed up.
care_protection_description: Defaults: pause at 40°C, reserve 8 GB on Mac and 4 GB on Pixel. Adjust these in Settings. Transfers pause at a protection limit and are checked again later.
care_progress_description: The app backs up unmodified originals, not edits or album structure. Keep the State progress folder. Backup identities belong to the source library.
care_honest_note: Automatic Mac staging cleanup is available. Per-file cloud verification and automatic Pixel cleanup are not available yet.

meta_title: PixelBridge — Another copy of your Apple Photos
meta_description: Send Apple Photos to Google Photos through your Mac and an original Pixel. Incremental transfers, motion photos, resumable progress and cache cleanup.
